subject: Multi-region performance evaluation — next steps and test ask
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Torres <leah.torres@nimble-retail.com>, Ahmed Khan <a.khan@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region performance evaluation — next steps and test ask

Hi Leah / Ahmed,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood:

- Scope: head-to-head inference comparisons across US-WEST1 (cloud gateway), EU-WEST1 (Frankfurt), AP-SOUTHEAST1 (Singapore). Models: your "retail-2b" quantized variant; compare Redwood hosted (default runtime), AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex.
- Success metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for 1/16/128/512 tokens; sustained throughput at 100 qps; cold-start latency; memory/kv cache hit rates; error rate under sustained load.
- Constraints: data residency requirement for EU-owned PII (store logs in EU S3 bucket); no model weights transferred off customer environment (NDA noted).

Action items we propose:
1) Nimble: share small representative prompt set (<=500 prompts) and a short test dataset for generation quality and latency.
2) Nimble: provide read-only S3 bucket + temporary creds (or presigned upload) for test outputs, and the IP allowlist range for traffic.
3) Redwood: run a 48-hour cross-region perf sweep and provide raw traces + aggregated dashboard + cost estimate.
4) Redwood SEs: produce a test matrix and estimated resource footprint; recommend whether Dedicated nodes are needed for parity with hyperscalers.

Attachments: call recording (nimble_call_20270403.mp4, link below).

Proposed timeline: start smoke test next Tue 2027-04-06; full 48-hour run Wed–Thu (2027-04-07 → 2027-04-08). Let us know availability.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-region performance evaluation — next steps and test ask

Plan below — will turn into a test matrix CSV and runbook (attached) and send to Nimble by 17:00 PT.

Test matrix (summary):
- Regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1
- Model variants: retail-2b (int8), retail-2b (fp16), retail-2b+kv (cache warmed)
- Token lengths: 1, 16, 128, 512
- Concurrency profiles: 1, 10, 50, 100 qps sustained; 500 qps spike for 5 min
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit rate, error rate

Execution plan:
- Smoke (1h) on 2027-04-06 to validate connectivity and auth using nimble S3.
- Full 48h sweep starting 2027-04-07 00:00 UTC; we'll spin Dedicated 1xA100-equivalent pool for parity runs and run hosted API runs to measure differences.
- Deliverables: raw traces (zip), aggregated dashboard link, CSV test matrix, cost delta summary for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Estimated infra cost (48h):
- Dedicated (1xA100 pool, network egress): ~$6,400
- Hosted API (per-token for equivalent load): ~$4,900
Notes: Dedicated gives lower p99 (expected ~10–20% improvement for warm cache) and deterministic throughput; hosted reduces operational burden but can have higher tail under cold workloads.

Attachments: redwood-test-matrix.csv (detailed matrix), runbook_testplan.md (run instructions)

I'll include a short section comparing to hyperscalers: we will run Bedrock and Vertex in parallel (Nimble to provide credentials) and ensure tokenization parity; highlight Redwood advantages: continuous batching, KV prefix cache, and ability to run Private for residency/weights.

-Karthik
